summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate (Rochester Institute of Technology) with hands-on bare-metal embedded C experience on STM32 Cortex-M4 microcontrollers, including FreeRTOS task coordination and direct GPIO/ADC/I2C peripheral programming for real-time constrained systems. Built and debugged custom hardware across SPI, I2C, and UART serial links using oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, backed by original schematic-driven PCB design in EAGLE. Integrated Bluetooth (BLE) connectivity for wireless sensor hardware and fabricated custom boards for field-deployed robots.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and Bluetooth (BLE/Classic) HC-05 hardware to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE from schematics and datasheets for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 temperature-monitoring firmware in bare-metal C for real-time operation on highly constrained microcontrollers, with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.

Programmed peripherals directly (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) from vendor datasheets and schematics with interrupt-driven ADC capture and a low-level I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on an STM32 controller driven over UART by interrupt-driven command parsing.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with user override and integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing (I2C) with OLED distance visualization.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
